text: January 2021: In short..I'm done, and moving on from any.do. What was one of my "go to" apps, solid 5 stars, is now unreliable, buggy, and all i hear from support is "well, our developers say thats 'intended behavior'..". Well, when new so-called intended behavior now makes the app more unreliable, to the point of unusable, its time to find a new app to replace any.do. And thats exactly what I'll be doing, and then pushing the "uninstall" button for any.do. November 2020: This was a 4-5 star app for me for years, but now since what appears to have happened during a major update in October, I can't give more than 3 stars. I'm posting this here in the hopes that maybe others are experiencing the same issue, and that will prompt more serious investigation by the any.do staff. The issue I am seeing occurs when setting a reminder for a future date. Go thru the usual process, app records the reminder date/time correctly, then sometimes minutes, or even seconds later, the reminder shows up as a current task under "today". Its happening intermittently, but at least 50% of the time. I've used any.do for several years, so I know its not a situation of not knowing how to use the app. Clearing data and cache and reinstalling has not helped. Any.do support is trying to help, wants a video, but I can't take a video of every time I set a reminder hoping to catch the issue. Its unrealistic. If anyone else using the app is experiencing this issue, please please please let Any.do support know. I won't discount its an issue specific to my device, but the fact that the app ran fine for years, until an update, has me thinking otherwise.

text: I purchased premium almost immediately, as this is exactly what I've been looking for - simple to-do lists. Can repeat tasks, can set reminders, can add subtasks, can colour code, can sync with calendar, can have several lists - or can just ignore all that and use a simple dump-it-all perpetually ongoing to-do list. Love it. Can also use it from desktop on any OS (web interface), and it syncs quickly. There's a light mode with several colours available, and also night mode with a black background. Separately I would like to mention customer service. I was stuck in another country due to the pandemic, and my card got blocked. My bank took its blissful time to reissue and send a new card to me - meanwhile, all my subscriptions and bills bounced. I got a billing issue notification. I replied, explaining my situation, and any.do was very kind to provide a month of premium usage for free. Priority support replies are very prompt. The agent I was in contact with (Tali) is polite and quick. Overall, this app is a keeper. Finally a todo app that I use - because it doesn't annoy me.

text:
This is an excellent app. I've been using it off and on for years. The only 
time I've ever uninstalled it was either when an update messed something 
up, or when I was super desperate for space on my phone, and I gotta say - 
my productivity has gone down each time. This app is one of the only 
successful things to get me to get things done. Despite health issues, lack 
of motivation among other things - for whatever reason, this app works. 
It's features are excellent too. I just re-installed this a few days ago 
and I see they finally added a reminders and adding tasks bar to the pull 
down menu on my phone - they also added a pretty nifty and usable widget 
(which is on my homescreen now tyvm!). The lack of these is one of the 
reasons I uninstalled before, so it's nice to see improvements. Add on to 
this that you can have multiple lists at once for free, you can add 
sub-tasks, notes and even attach photos and other types of files to your 
to-do's.. yet another improvement from the last version, and one of the 
only apps to offer these amazing features for free. Then of course add to 
all of these wonderful features the basics, that you can add alarm 
reminders or even calendar reminders. You can combine an alarm reminder 
with a pop up reminder. You can add a combination calendar with your 
appointments and task list with your to-do's right to your homescreen - and 
it's not an ugly one either (though this one isn't quite so basic)! I 
highly recommend this app - if you can get the paid version, all the better!

text:
Don't let three stars dissuade you from trying it. Any.do is an absolutely 
gorgeous app, very well polished, and replete with great features. Probably 
among the best task apps if you are the kind of user that creates task 
lists in a vacuum. I would love this as a stand alone solution. But for a 
large subset of users (including myself) poor to non-existent Google 
integration makes it a non starter. Two way sync with Google calendar is 
cumbersome, and in order to get decent functionality requires using 
any.do's in app calendar tapping into your phone's stock calendar and 
usually requires tweaking categories and reminders after the fact. You can 
forget proper integration with Gmail, and while any.do supports a set of 
skills for Alexa, any.do does not allow Google assistant to tap into voice 
commands for managing tasks. Even if the developers bring their proprietary 
voice assistant to Android at some point, those who run a Google ecosystem 
with multiple devices will cringe at being unable to interface with 
assistant. There is no question that any.do outshines the competition in 
intuitiveness. I spent hours trying to figure out how to make integration 
work for me -almost resorting to some pretty janky ITTT recipes, because 
the app is so clean and straightforward. It spelled out how to use features 
I wanted so well that when I tried other apps to compare I didn't even 
realize they had some of the same features buried in the UI (location based 
reminders, repeating reminders, even at odd intervals, etc - the only one I 
really loved and couldn't get elsewhere was call back tasks for missed 
calls.) This really speaks to any.do's commitment to a great user 
experience. And their notifications make it super easy to manage tasks by 
rescheduling or snoozing with a bare minimum of user actions required. In 
the end, however, I had to choose something that worked well with the 
"exosystem" I use and wound up as a premium user of todoist, which shares 
any.do's most important freatures, is cheaper, and integrates very well 
with Google products, even if it is far less elegant.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Thank you for the detailed review Jordan! We appreciate your comments and agree that an integration with Google's Assistant is the next step. We hope to be able to work on it with the Google Team just like we did with the Amazon Team :) We're already in touch and are exploring our options for collaboration in the near future 😉

text: Premium review! *read carefully*  Tried this app before version 4.0 and now we are in 4.9 and the issues that many people had before are still quite prevalent. That being said, integrating Cal and tasks was a big step up and the AI has certainly improved. But, the UI still doesn't seem anywhere close to worth the $50 a year.   1. STILL no switching between calendar views (week, month, agenda, etc)  2. Overall customization is very very very basic 3. There should be calendar and task combined widgets with customizing features much like DigiCal and other competitors 4. At the bottom of the apps home screen there is a choice between settings, tasks, and calendar but it should be a persistent bar and the settings should be on the far left.   5. When you have the 6 day or month view(only views available) there should be color, animation, something that shows you have something coming up of that category(ie red=personal,  green=pay bills).   *6. Kind of a really big one...  This is supposed to be a calendar, to-do list, reminder, planner. You are required to enter a time/date when entering a task(I'm guessing that's the to-do list). If this is the case, and I could be wrong, it sounds like a slightly smarter calendar app than most. Setting a task that's required to have a time even tho they simplified it to 3 times a day(or custom time) is still just a just appointment.    There is nothing(other than Alexa integration) this app can do that I can't do with a to-do list app(todoist) and a calendar app(DigiCal) integration and pay ZERO DOLLARS.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Any.do does offer a widget combining both calendar and tasks :) Also, tasks do not require a date when added directly to the 'someday' category or dragged and dropped there. We keep the Calendar View simple on purpose to go along with our minimalistic design. However, we appreciate the feedback and will pass it on to our Product Team.

text: To the core, this is not a To-Do app. This seems to be designed entirely as a scheduler, with dates cluttering the interface and no apparent way to disable them if you want solely a checklist. The interface is often confusing: e.g. instead of providing a "done" button for the daily reminder screen, you have to hit the back button, which gives the user no guarantee that their input will be saved. Screens will be locked for premium accounts, but give no indication that's why they're locked. If you click on the sillouette of a locked screen, it takes you to a cycling roulette describing the premium package, but has no title or other indication of what that screen is; it's  just a roulette with seemingly random text.  Overall this app sports a confusing interface that demands it's users adjust to it, and lacks a clear direction- coming out part-way between a To-Do and scheduler app without fulfilling either role completely. The premium service may fare better, but what it boasts is available more polished elsewhere.

text: Any.Do is incredibly user friendly and easy to use. It's not in the way during normal phone use but immediately accessible when you're on the go and need it now. Had to create a new one which is tedious when there are numerous subtasks, specific dates to look up again, yadda yadda. So I hit up support through their app. Tali on their support team responded promptly, informed me that a fix was already in the works for the next update, and if I wanted, the beta version (sign up in Settings > Any.Do Community > Be a Super User) had the fix implemented already. Sure did! And it worked great. Fast forward a month later, today, and Tali emails me a follow-up just to let me know the update to fix the issue I had was publicly released and available for download. My jaw dropped.  Idk if that sounds like much to you, but to get such personalized support for an issue that for most support teams would have considered closed and forgotten, I mean I already had a satisfactory resolution.. to get that extra cherry on top was just wow!  Love the app. Love the support. I highly recommend just trying the thing if you're scrolling through reviews right now. Totally worth it.

I also thought there would be more settings in priority but it only allows "high" and "normal", which isn't very useful. Plus it pushes users to buy the premium version whatever you do. The only thing I like is the notification bar - it shows in the notification when you pull it down but doesn't show an icon and so doesn't clutter it up - and the fact that you can add your own categories. text: I didn't like this app. It doesn't offer anything more than my phone calendar and in some ways less. The only feature that I liked was the daily planning reminder though I didn't quite get his to set it for a time I wanted so it popped up at an inconvenient time. Even so , I'm not the kind of person who wants to enter "check my email" every single day and feel like I've planned. I'd rather enter it once and tell the app to do for a duration, say every daily for six months. Entering it daily becomes a waste of time for me, especially when the marking it complete deletes it. This app is great if you need help developing the habit of time management, but I wouldn't call it a to time management tool. Good place to start when you're totally undisciplined or struggling, but frustrating after you have the hang of it. You want the time spent planning to be productive, not a waste or it becomes counterproductive.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: We appreciate your honest feedback, and agree that some productivity apps are better suited for specific individuals. We understand Any.do may not have been best suited for you, but definitely agree it's suitable for those who need productivity boosts in their daily lives.

text: Using the premium version of Any.do for several days makes me realize why I could never stick to Google Calendar and paper planners while in college. They blur the line between tasks and events. Tasks are time-indepedent. A calendar event is time or situation sensitive and requires you to be at a particular place at a particular time and occasionally with someone. It's possible to turn off the reminder, but the design of any.do tasks makes me feel like I have to a certain tasks at certain times and I'd fail if I don't.  Another problem is that the snooze option sounds like a fantastic idea on paper but inefficient in practice. It makes me develop the bad habit of ignoring the text and just hitting snooze. The four options are unnecessary IMO, as it's from my observation and what I've learned of willpower and energy is that if you don't an important task now, it'd only get harder to do it as each hour passes by.

text: I tried Any.do out when I realized that my current to-do manager of choice was getting to be a bit more than I wanted to spend. However, Any.do doesn't yet have one feature that's really important to me: the ability to input the due date quickly via typing or voice. For example, being able to type or say, "Return library book in 2 weeks," or, "pick up cookies on Friday," hitting a single button to save, and having the software assign the proper date. This is much faster than having to click several times. If Any.do gains this feature that my current to-do manager has already had for some time, I'll give it a more serious look. However, Any.do does shine when it comes to entering tasks that fit the categories of today, tomorrow, or no due date.

Given what's happened since, it's ironic to read those words again before editing my comment. First of all there was 'bloat creep'. Features I didn't need or want, making the app take up more and more space on my phone. Also it seemed to be increasingly buggy! I had several repeat reminders that stopped repeating on the correct day - I had to keep editing them each week. Then I learn this repeat feature (along with others) is now a premium option only. Hmm, maybe that's why it's not working any more? And premium? Ok I can live with that, I think. But it'll cost WHAT?? $27 USD every year??!! And ... you're kidding!  ... that's actually HALF PRICE for a LIMITED TIME??!! No way! Not when other apps will do what I want far less expensively. I believe in supporting developers and always pay for apps I find useful if they have that option. But NOT for one that's both bloated and horrendously overpriced.

text: Any.do was a good task manager that could do pretty much anything you would've wanted it to do; set reminders, sync between devices, share tasks with others, and so on.  Then they decided to offer premium services.  Now, I've got nothing against that -- I've paid for plenty of apps -- but the problem is that they decided to strip out basic features that were previously free and make you pay for them.  This includes basic things like changing the color scheme from light to dark.  And it's not a one time fee; it's a monthly or yearly subscription.  Sorry, but I'm not going to support a company who thinks it's ok to take previously free, basic features and require a subscription to access them.

The Any.Do Moment is a good feature -- except that it sometimes makes me deal twice with an item that has a dated reminder on it. That's a bit irritating. I'd like to see an option to have the app display upcoming items in date order. One of Any-Do's best features is the ability to sync with my desktop machine, and they've added a web app to do that so that the lack of a Firefox extension is no longer much of an issue. text: I tried quite a few todo apps before settling for Any.Do. It had a lot of potential. Sadly, it turned out to be a major disappointment. For all the bells and whistles it offers, Any.Do fails to do the one thing properly it was supposed to do - manage my todo tasks. Here are my top 4 gripes:  (1). Why do all tasks have time associated with them? Planning a day is hard and predicting the time for each task during the day is even harder. Forcing the user to attach time with a task is a sign of shortsightedness in the developers. Every time I edit a task, I have to manually remove its alarm. It's really annoying. (2). Every time I open the app, it tries to sync with the server. If my data connection is flaky, it does not show any items at all because it cannot finish the sync. That is also very annoying. Why not let the sync happen in the background and let me use the app right away? (3). The "Upcomig" category is useless. The tasks could be due next week or in 2 months - there is no way to differentiate. There should be at least a way to look at tasks due next week. (4). Moving a task around is very cumbersome. Dragging one from "Today" to "Someday" needs a lot of patience and skill.

It took me ten minutes to figure out that you delete with a swipe.  Oh, ha ha, I get it, you're a bunch of iOS developers trying to sell into the android market.  FAIL.    There are other things that are just simply broken.  For example, if you have a recurring alert, and it goes off at its standard time of (say) 10:00 am, and you hit the snooze button...what time do you expect it to go off tomorrow?  At 10:00 am?  Obviously you're a simpleton and not a genius like the any.do developers, who have decided that what you REALLY want is to have the alert time changed for the future to 10 AM plus some random number of minutes.  And wow, the adorableness, no, not lovin' that either.  It's not clever, it's just cutesy, and it's definitely not functional.  It is a WASTE OF TIME, all these stupid little "congratulations" messages.  Stop wasting time on stupid useless stuff like that and develop an app that works.

text: Any.do is an app that goes beyond what other productivity apps have achieved. First of all, the interface on all platforms is absolutely amazing, it is user-friendly and makes task organization a pleasure rather than a chore. On top of it, it is very well integrated with Google Chrome (as well as Google Keep) and Android devices. Overall, has set the new standard in the world of productivity apps.   However, Any.do seems to be ridden with all kinds of minor problems that sometimes make the user experience absolutely terrible.  First of all, there seems to be a permanent synchronization problem even between the two different desktop apps, and not even to mention between PC and Android; on one you would add a new task and the same task would simply not show on the other, or show much later.  Second, there seem to be persistent bugs in the system- at least on HTC Sensation- that prevent you from deleting tasks or marking them as done.   Any.do is amazing, and I would award it five stars if it wasn't for persisting problems that never seem to get fixed and that seriously deteriorate the user experience.

text: This app is really pretty.  Unfortunately, syncing across devices is terrible.  Also, the reminder system needs serious work for this to be as revolutionary as the hype-text.  I just manually started the app this morning (after it missed my "any.do moment") and it downloaded a slew of tasks I had added through the chrome extension (not Google Tasks) the night before.  Prior to this the reminders would collide with each other and seemed to come from a different app entirely.  I would complete a task early and mark it, but several hours later I would get its reminder.  I would plan for a task to be done at 4pm today, but get the reminder 30 minutes later when its old due time came around.  I would be running a little ahead of schedule, hit the plan button to go through my tasks and then after I finished I would get the "any.do moment" pop-up even though I had just planned my day five minutes earlier.  For any app that seems to really think it will make you live better this app isn't nearly as smart as it needs to be.

text: This app is good for quick task management, but does not meet full task management functionalities.  As it is, I would have to use two task managers - one for serious work (projects and business type tasks) and this one for those items that come up and fall out (meaning I would never search for it at a later date).  I would prefer one task management application.  This app has tremendous promise.  I especially like the auto completion functionality, as well as the ability to directly act on a task (bring up Contact record for the person I've identified to either text or call, navigation and others).  I would use this application as my "go-to" manager if two things would happen; 1. Better note handling (single line notes are a pain to enter and work with). 2. ToodleDo integration vs Google Tasks.  The absence of a desktop app also hurts, but with ToodleDo, I could use other desktop apps.  Great start, and I hope to see improvements on the items I've listed.  I would love to use this as my task manager of choice.

text: Any.Do quickly became one of the leading Android to-do managers. It began as a nice way to use Google Tasks, and has now eclipsed it. Its shining achievement so far is the "Any.do Moment", which helps you review and schedule your day. Any.do looks good, but the slick drag & drop interface bogs down when you have a lot of tasks to move around. Still, it's very usable and easy to update. The GMail integration is great, and the Android version can create actionable tasks like "Call Fred" or "Email Fred" and let you execute it directly (but the actions embedded in these tasks don't sync). Each note added to a task doubles as a checklist item that can be crossed off, which is handy. These don't surface as independent tasks in any view. Also, completed tasks are not tracked or monitored, and just hang around, unlike Todoist's excellent Karma system.  Still, Any.Do is a great choice if you can live without multiple priorities, subtasks or tracking of completed tasks.

text: Overall, it's a pretty good application, and if you intend to use it by yourself it's great. However the sharing features are somewhat broken and need a lot of work. If you intend to use it to share tasks and lists, don't expect a very good experience. I'm giving it such a bad rating because I use Any-Do almost exclusively for the sharing features, so with these bugs it makes it almost unusable for me.  First off, there are no shared lists, only shared tasks. I would prefer to be able to share a whole list and have it synced between two people instead of having to share individual tasks.  Also, sharing tasks is buggy. For example: sometimes I get a share request in my notifications bar, touch it and then don't actually get any message in Any-Do that lets me accept the task. This would be forgivable if there was a way to see all the pending shared-tasks that you never accepted, or a way to see all tasks that have ever been shared with you, but there no way to do this.  Also, there is no way to mark a task as complete for everyone a task is shared with. You mark it complete for yourself and the other people must mark it complete separately.

Mass action, move multiple items from one folder to another, complete many items at once, etc.  2. Item drag mechanic and animation are very glitchy.  Dragging an item up or down is very painful as the screen doesn't auto scroll causing the user to have to start and stop.  3. Slide to delete or un-delete does not have an associated animation during the slide action.  For a new user this is poor design as a user may not even realize the slide action is there since there is no visual feedback during the slide action.  3a. Most "click" or "touch" user actions do not have any visual animation or feedback.  Also poor UI design.  4. (Minor) Does not respect hierarchy of Google Tasks.  I often have a parent-child task relationship, this is not synced / supported by Any.do.  These are just the 4 things I've noticed in my first 10 minutes using the app.  Haven't given up yet but some pretty glaring improvements are necessary.

Maybe you could also add an option to move tasks during the daily planning so it would actually make sense to have an "Inbox" folder.  - Even creating a task in a specific folder isn't all that easy. text: Visually stunning but lacks in functinality for a truly useful To-Do app	Love the look and feel of the app.  Definitely the most eye catching and visually cool "to-do" app out there that I've tried (previously favorite was Toodledo or related 3rd party Toodledo apps).  The coolest things are the alerts, how they pop up if you miss a call or when a task is due.  However, there are few major things that are lacking that will likely discourage me from using it as my go to to-do app.  1. Limited repeat options: you cannot repeat an event or task other than "day, week, month, year."  So if you want to have a repeating task every 3 months, there does not appear to be a way to do that. 2. Same thing for reminders: if I have a due date for a task 2 months from now, there is currently no way to set a reminder 2 weeks before the deadline. 3. On the homepage, although simple and elegant bird's eye view of your tasks, it is missing simple dates next to each task.  The most useful to-do apps I find have this...otherwise, I have to remember or guess when something is due or click on it to find out when the task is exactly due.  Due to these major flaws, I am rating it 3 stars, but if they add these features, I would not hesitate to give them 5 stars.

text: I am one of the many former befuddled Astrid users looking for a new home. I loved the look and feel of Any.do and I hoped that it could provide what I need, but the lack of anything but the most basic support for recurring tasks makes it a non-starter for me. At a minimum, I need the ability to:  * Recur tasks at arbitrary intervals, such as "every other day" or "every 3 months" * Set particular days within an interval, such as "every day except Saturday and Sunday" * Set the due date of the subsequent task based on either the due date or the completed date of the current task * Snooze reminders at any arbitrary interval, or *at least* be able to customize the offered intervals  I don't want to crap on Any.do too much for features that it doesn't have and may very well be coming soon. I wanted very much to continue using it because the UI is wonderful and the Moment feature is genius. But my workflow is more granular and specific than Any.do allows me to be.

SHOWING THE DUE DATE CHALLENGES THE USER TO COMPLETE THE TASK  2) Any Do should also include activity/goal formation.     For example, if i want to do certain activity, say learn drawing. text: I think this app is one of the best - and easiest to use - app to manage to-do's. One of the best but not the best.  It has a clean and simple interface (white or black, with an uncluttered graphic design) and great features (reminders with snooze and reschedule, daily planning exercise, Google Chrome and Tasks integration, ...).  However, it doesn't seem to handle well too many items or too many lists   Let me explain: it is no possible to effectively group items by category. Folders exists, but if one displays tasks by deadline, the folders are not taken into account. Also, it is not possible to show (either in the widget or in the app itself, tasks from a single folder.  What would really help here is the ability to categorize and display tasks by both folder (and subfolder) and due date.  Second issue, in my opinion, is to implement sub-tasks and/or order tasks (ideally both).  With the two functions above, Any.do would be able to handle more and larger to-do lists in a very beautiful way. Without it, one risks to be lost.

text: I have been testing quite a few task management applications lately and I keep returning to Any.Do. My huge downfall with task apps is that I put in the tasks, but I forget to check them, and I procrastinate often. Any.Do helps me with both issues by planning my day first thing in the morning and reminding me about things throughout the day. I also really like the missed call integration, it is perfect!  I do believe that some of the design of the app could be better, like the popup when you edit a task, the text is HUGE and doesn't wrap, for instance. I'm also curious how a Holo based interface would work out. And the Widget isn't that great (way to much white space, need to see more tasks in a smaller area). Lastly, I think that the Notes feature is good, but it is not a replacement for true sub-tasks. I do not understand why it is so hard to find a service that offers true sub-tasking. It would also be nice to reorder Notes. I only mention these things because I believe it is currently the best task manager out and I want to see it continue to grow!

I can add/delete/edit items from Outlook, my phone, or Google Calendar and sync and it is in all three places.  This program has kept me on top of my schedule and it does it with ease.  The various widgets that are available for my phone and tablet allow me maximum flexibility on how I want to interact with it.  I was willing to pay to help support this app but after emailing the development team all they said was thanks for the kind words.  WHAT . . . kind words, that is the least I could do. text: I've been looking for a good ToDo app for a while, and the problem I found with most of them is that it's a hassle to keep the todo list up to date. It's almost like, instead of actually doing things, I just waste time keeping my list up to date - adding, removing, rescheduling items, etc. With Any.DO it's no longer a chore. As long as you have some items on the agenda it will occasionally, gently remind you about them, and offer a very quick and intuitive way to update them - move some to another day, set reminders for some for an hour or two later, mark some as done, etc. All of this is presented in such a slick and beautiful interface that it's a pleasure to update the items and only takes seconds.  In short, if you're looking for a great todo app, Any.DO is it.

text: The Good: Beautiful interface. Love the option to integrate missed calls and callbacks into to-do flow. New "Plan" feature is good for leading you through a high-altitude view of upcoming tasks, and allowing you to reprioritize as conditions change.  The Bad: The controls to sync with your Google tasks are at least three menu/button pushes away from the main screen. Then, once you have found your way to the sync screen and synced up with your Gogole tasks, it leaves you in that screen instead of immediately taking you back to the main screen, so you have to hit the back button 3 times to get back. I consider Google task sync central to the functionality of the app, but the devs apparently think otherwise. On competing task apps (e.g., GTasks) the sync button is on the main screen where it should be. This would be at least a 4-star app if the devs would wake up and understand that Google task sync is a big deal.  The Ugly: whatever it is that this app is supposed to accomplish with the Chrome extension. There's no documentation for it and through two-three upgrades of the app and the extension I have never been able to get it working through trial and error.

Also if you have recurring tasks at a specific time and you snooze a reminder 15 minutes for example, ALL future occurrences of this task get pushed back 15 minutes, not just the current one it's reminding you about. text: I really want to use this App. I think the interface and the categorization are excellent.  But a task scheduling and reminder app that can't handle time zones and puts your tasks on the wrong date?  When tasks are synced to Google tasks and shared across devices I understand that the reminder time will not sync because Google Tasks don't have time specific reminders. But at a minimum the date should sync properly. In Any.Do this does not work. The tasks are synced to GMT and then offset on the device by the time zone.  So if you are in the eastern time zone (Canada and US) -5 hrs for example your tasks will sync to 19:00hrs the day before they are due. This is an acknowledged bug and they are "checking into it". If you use this app on a single device and don't sync it to Google Tasks it works very well.  If you plan to use it across devices and sync it, it quickly looses its appeal with tasks showing up as due when they aren't. Showing as due tomorrow when they aren't due until the following day.  Showing the wrong date when checking on an upcoming task. Sure you can remember that the dates are wrong...   Also, 4 menu taps to navigate in order to sync... have to do better.

It's visually far nicer than gTasks, the app I've been using in conjunction with Google Tasks, but syncing between the app and the Chrome extension or either of those and Google Tasks just doesn't work very well. I'd have to manually sync in order for things I entered into the phone app to show up in the extension, vice versa, or either onto Google, and every time I synced with Google, I got duplication of many other tasks. It also doesn't treat sub-tasking the same way as Google, keeping them as notes rather than nested tasks. I prefer Google's integration much more, since nested tasks are still visible, while the notes are hidden until you click on the main task.   In the end, I'll stick with "ugly but it works" over "pretty but unreliable" when it comes to a lists app.

text: After testing four other To-do apps I came back to Any.DO because it has the functionality I like; especially its integration with my Contact manager and voice recognition.   There are a few things I'd like to see improved however: 1.  Autosync - there's currently no way to automatically sync with Google Tasks 2.  Themes -  The app has only two themes; Light and Dark.  For people who customize their devices extensively this is rather limiting. 3.  Widgets - The appearance of the current widgets are linked to the theme selected in the app.  Ideally the widgets' appearance should be independent and be easily adjusted.  I'd also love to see the ability to adjust the transparency/opacity of the widget to allow it to better blend into customized home screens. Also, adding a Sync icon to the widgets would be a huge time-saver since that would eliminate the need to go to the app and go through four layers of menus to get to the sync function.

text: There are hundreds of task management apps and programs out there. The bad ones are usually nothing more than a notepad in fancy clothes. With a few notable exceptions, the popular ones tend to be much more complex - A LOT more complex. While I appreciate the complexity and sophistication of some of the top task managing services out there like Astrid, I have also found that complexity gets in the way of me actually doing the tasks. I end up spending hours every week obsessing over the state of my tasks and events. So I want simplicity, but something more than is offered by the glorified notepad...  Any.Do has really struck a near-perfect balance. It allows multiple ways to sort, parse and view your tasks - it even allows for subtasks (which is great for those of us who like to take on ambitious projects). In the end, however, any.do maintains a since of purity that really resonates with me.   Any.Do is by far the best task manager I have ever used. The UI is immaculate and it's cross-platform support of google tasks, Chrome, HTML5 (coming soon!) and iOS make it excellent. Throw the ability to recruit others to help you and you've got a real winner!

text: I typically don't use "to do" lists because they're rarely convenient, but after a few days using Any.Do I find myself staying on task more and accomplishing my immediate goals more quickly. In the last 10 minutes I knocked-out three tasks that might easily have lingered on my list for days.  Here are the highlights: Easily pulls from your contacts when you need to send an email or return a call Integrates across devices and products (Gmail, Contacts, Calander, etc.) even in the Chrome browser Allows for notes and file attachments  I haven't been able to figure out how to duplicate a task or set it to recur, but I'm sure the functionality's there if I really looked into it.  I highly recommend Any.do if you need an app that will keep you more organized and improve your productivity.

text: Minimally designed and beautiful interface, but it falls short honestly on features.  I use Google tasks extensively in the sidebar of Google calendar when I'm at my desk, and then when I'm on the move I open up a task app to get things done.  Any.DO just doesn't display the tasks as expected.  - no auto sync - no nested tasks; if you create groups within lists with nested members, Any.DO just throws it all in one long list; it doesn't maintain the hierarchy - there are two default lists -  'Personal' and 'Work' - which CANNOT be changed.  One of my lists (by a different name) is always synced to the 'Personal' list in Any.DO - why can't we rename these two default lists, or delete them altogether?  While the interface is simple and beautiful, for my purposes, gTasks works much better. It doesn't look as nice, but it's way more functional. BTW I have no affiliation with gTasks at all.  Cheers

text: This app is useful, but could be much better.  It seems all about conveying an overly simplified, "iPhone-like" style.  The layout is so wasteful of space -- you could compress 75% more onto a screen, requiring less scrolling around to find items.  But that would interfere with that "cool relaxed" look that appears to be the main priority.  Also, what's with the stupid "shake to clear items" thing?  And the animated line when you cross things off?  It's all about gimmicks, not about getting things done.  Here's what I need -- hopefully there's an app out there that:  -Lets you squeeze more items to a page, do stuff like color coding etc -Lets you undo an "I accomplished this item" action (what's the point of it sitting there, grayed-out, if you can't undo it??) -Lets you sort in a more complex way than either by priority, or by date.  In real life, many actions are "get to them as soon as possible", but many others are "not urgent, but needs doing by July 20".  I need to see both of these at once, not make a choice between two simplistic sort methods. -Lets you select multiple items to easily sort your list.  Dragging one at a time, when you have 30 items, is way too much trouble.

text: I decided recently to go over how I have my phone set up as it has been a long time since I last made any changes. I had Astrid installed with their widget, but other than a few times I have never really used it. As part of my decision making I installed a bunch of Task apps (Astrid, GTasks, Tasks N Todos) and gave them all a try and compared the features to one another. While each one has their advantages and disadvantages Any.DO stood out as the most refined of the bunch. First off the clean simple design makes it very pleasant to the eye to create, delete, modify, and monitor tasks. I am using this for personal tasks, which typically are not very elaborate complicated things, and a simple clear interface that shows me whats important is what I want and what this does. If I ever have tasks that require something more complicated to keep organized, well there is Evernote, Note Everything, Microsoft OneNote, or Google Docs; but frankly for simple reminders and tasks that do not require complex additional detail, this is perfect.  My one suggestion for improvement is that it should automatically sync with GMail. Still deserves 5 stars.

text: It is really a great app. I had been using quite a few of todo apps before I stuck with this one. It is an extremely straightforward, has a very, very intuitive interface, requires very few actions to set a task with some important attributes such as reminder, folder (can serve as a project) and priority.Dragging and dropping feature facilitate  quick rearrangements of the tasks. Swiping out completed task is amazing and gives much better satisfaction than ticking it out. Altogether lovely interface, elegancy and simplicity give me a kind of a feeling that it is not an app but it is like a part of my brain.  What I think would be useful is for each task to show below it in a small font the date (and time if it is set). Than scrolling over the tasks  in a sorting mode “by date” when we come to the tasks in folders "This week" and "Later"  we can see the assigned dates for them.  Also, integration with Pure Calendar Widget or any other calendar widget would be helpful, or maybe to design its own.

text: I really wanted this app to work out, but I'm uninstalling tonight.  This is the smoothest, slickest, best-looking To Do app I've found. I also liked the app's "date" headings of Today, Tomorrow, This Week, and Later.  These are all I really need.   I am finally giving up on it, though.  Its sync with Google Tasks was very, very buggy with ICS (granted, the last update seems to have largely fixed this).  Also, undated tasks automatically show up under "Today", at the top, with no option to either hide undated tasks or at least move them to the "Later" heading (that is, without having to manually drag every single one).  There were too many other little annoyances to describe here, related to sorting/displaying Google Task lists and individual tasks.  The widget could use more options, too, but this was relatively minor compared to the other problems with Google Tasks integration.    Even though I'm uninstalling now, this app's potential will have me checking back several months from now to see if it is more usable.

text: I initially really loved this app, but a couple of things irritated me. It is still the best task apps I've tried, so I thought it was worth passing on my thoughts...  Firstly, the information density is really low, especially in the widgets. For example, a 4x4 widget only shows a day at a time, so if there is only one task today you just get that and a big space. In the app itself you have to tap each one to find out any details, whereas simple icons would be good for reminders or notes like there is for emails and calls. I like how clean all the white (or black )space makes things, but I'd prefer to see more information.  Secondly, I loved the predictive stuff for building tasks, but not at the expense of my phone's keyboard's own predictive abilities. I use swiftkey and am very used to it correcting all sorts of common typing mistakes; I would prefer that over the app second guessing me.

On the server, it took every single individual task from a folder named "Work" and created a new folder for each one, also called "Work". I cannot move items back into a single folder or delete any of them.  On the phone, there is only one Work folder.  However, it duplicated another folder on the phone, called "Personal". Now there are two, one with content, one without. When I called up the folder list, neither of these folders can be deleted. All the others can. I renamed the second of these folders "delete me"; after syncing with Google, it didn't appear on the server, so I couldn't delete it there, either.  Temporarily I moved all the Work items into a new folder and deleted all the extra ones on the server. The new folder showed up on Any.do fine.  Tried clearing the data - the "delete me" folder disappeared - but the "Personal" folder came back, even though I have no Google Tasks folder named Personal any more.  Too much of a mess. I've uninstalled, I'm afraid.  Looks pretty, though, so two stars for that.

text: Any.DO is beautifully designed and a pleasure to use. Unfortunately it has some big problems.  The design is gorgeous. Simple and intuitive, and the best-looking app I've come across. That pleasure of use quickly encouraged me to move from a couple of tasks today to planning my week and beyond (in Google Tasks). Then I hit problems.  1. Sync with Google Tasks failed. At first intermittently, then on every sync. This made the app unusable. (There's been an update since; they may have fixed this.)  The only feedback was "Something went wrong, try again later", so I couldn't figure out if one of my tasks was breaking it.  2. Date control is very basic. I can set a task for 'Today' or 'Tomorrow', but for anything further out I have to settle for 'This Week' or 'Later'. To set a task for 'the day after tomorrow' I have to use Google.  3. A task in Google without a date shows up in Any.DO under Today. That's almost the opposite meaning - a real pain.  4. You can't filter multiple Google task lists. In Any.DO they all appear as a single list.  I've moved to another app that isn't half as nice but at least works properly. But I really do love Any.DO, and I hope they sort out the problems.

text: Others have said it: beautiful interface (and nice choice of typography), simple and clean and elegant. Everything a task manager/to-do list should be. I love it.  That said, there are a couple of glaring weak spots. The widget, at least on my tablet, has odd sizing. It takes up a 3x3 space, but the widget itself is much smaller (closer to 2x2). So it ends up having a lot of blank space around it, which (to me) is kind of wasteful. Also, it prevents those of us with OCD from lining it up properly with other widgets!  The other annoyance is the lack of flexibility for organizing. You can choose to sort by date, folder, or priority, but you can't change the settings within. So if you choose to sort by folder, you have "Personal" and "Work." Period. You can't change those. Choosing to sort by priority gives you "Urgent" and "No Rush." Period.   So there needs to be some mechanism for adding or customizing folders or priorities, as well as either resizing the widget or choosing from a selection of sizes.  That may sound like I have real problems with Any.DO, but I don't. It's really great, but needs to take that one small, extra step to perfection.

text: I have used ta-da by 37-signals, google tasks, outlook tasks, task paper, remember the milk and tons of others that I don't even remember. I am still actively using RTM for over an year now and am really liking it. I know 25$ isn't a huge amount, but having a free app on the phone is awesome. Any.do has a very nice interface and is very responsive. Haven't had any issues with crashes or the app freezing or nething. That being said, I would like for them to implement the same level of features that RTM has, namely, being able to set custom recurrence patterns for tasks.  For example, if I want a task to repeat on Mondays, Wednesday and Saturdays, I would have to create 3 separate tasks in any.do, whereas its a single task in RTM with a recurrence pattern for mon, wed and sat. Also, if I don't complete a task on a certain day that it should be completed on, I would rather that go into a "overdue" bin rather than just get carried over to the current day with no indication as to what the status of that task is.  All in all, this is an awesome app and I am assuming the above stated features are probably in the pipeline for a later release.  My Phone : Samsung Galaxy S2
